entry: (B) Codon routes into and out of lysine. E to K ranks first of 363 observed substitution pairs at 181,252 sites, 4.12% of all missense; context-corrected enrichment 1.12-fold, against 3.59, 3.38 and 3.16 for R to H, R to C and R to Q. Lysine is gained 85.5% by C>T and lost 0% by C>T. Rust marks the C>T routes, which are G:C to A:T changes, half of all cancer missense mutation. No C>T route leaves lysine because AAA carries no G or C, and the only G to A available to AAG gives AAA, which is still lysine. Arrow width increases with the share shown beside it.

entry: **(A) Four peptide species can carry an acquired-lysine site, and only two contain it.** One real site, written out in full: LDHB E287K in NCIH1793, [K].GMYGIENK[287]VFLSLP​CILNAR.[G]. Bracketed residues outside the periods are the flanking residues in the protein and are not part of the peptide; the bracketed number is the position of the acquired lysine in UniProt P07195. Residues 280–299 are a single tryptic peptide of 20 residues in the wild-type protein. The acquired lysine, marked in orange on the two species that carry it, subdivides that peptide into an 8-residue mutant peptide and a 12-residue downstream peptide; the missed-cleavage form spans all 20, and the bars are drawn on one residue pitch so their lengths are those counts. Sequences and lengths are computed by digesting P07195 with and without the substitution, not transcribed. The mutant peptide and its missed-cleavage form carry the mutated residue; the downstream peptide and the wild-type peptide do not. An acquired lysine creates a tryptic cleavage site, so the mutant peptide has different boundaries from the wild-type peptide; the two are not one sequence with a letter changed. That same new boundary is what releases the downstream peptide, which therefore carries no mutated residue and still exists only in the mutant protein, and is why it can report a site it does not contain. For an E→K site the mutant is heavier by 303.26 Da once the new lysine carries TMTpro, with different hydrophobicity and charge state. **This site is an instance of the asymmetry the figure is about, not an illustration of it:** across the 42 plexes the 20-residue wild-type peptide was never observed and the 8-residue mutant peptide was, which places LDHB E287K among the 26 of 7,853 uncovered sites in panel C.

entry: (B) Margin dose-response over 1,489 rows, counted as distinct peptides. The false-discovery proportion is 4.70% at margin 0, 1,419 variant peptides against 70 entrapment, and falls to 3.91% at a margin of 2, 2.36% at 5 and 0.83% at 10, where 832 variant peptides survive against seven entrapment. Past a margin of 15 only one entrapment peptide remains, so the rate there reflects a single count rather than a cleaner set. A 1% reported false-discovery rate is not a 1% realized one for this class of peptide unless a margin is applied. Restricted to the acquired-lysine class the proportion is bounded at 7.9% by the rule of three, with the counts and the comparison against the rest of the variant class in Extended Results.

entry: (D) Median spectral-quality features for the 38 acquired-lysine identifications expressed relative to 802,067 background spectra from 20 of the 77 runs in the same searches, so 1.0 is the background. Peak count 0.91-fold, signal-to-noise 1.19-fold, from medians of 631 against 695 peaks and 0.221 against 0.185. These features score a spectrum on its own properties, with no reference to the search engine, the database or the false-discovery rate. The plus one dalton tail accounts for 7.7% of variant and 7.3% of background spectra. SQS$_{GM}$ is omitted because the MGF export zeroed its intensity term, which would collapse a geometric mean.

entry: **(D) The gate, step by step.** Four representative features' reactivity effect at each rung. The strip beneath each rung is what that rung keeps, drawn to scale against the ungated 245,684 lysines, with the labeled share as the dark segment: none 245,684 of which 30,805 labeled (246k on the figure, 100% kept, 13% labeled), ≥ 50 189,913 of which 28,316 (190k, 77%, 15%), ≥ 70 167,057 of which 25,979 (167k, 68%, 16%), ≥ 90 97,722 of which 17,409 (98k, 40%, 18%). Charge features hold or strengthen across the ladder; shape features fall. The gate therefore costs 60% of all lysines by its tightest rung while raising the labeled share from 13% to 18%, so the two groups do not shrink at the same rate.

entry: (E) The permutation test, over the gate ladder and against the null. Two stacked axes. Agreement is the correlation, across the features of one kind, between a feature's effect on reactivity and its effect on ligandability. The upper axis is that agreement as the gate tightens: charge stays at 0.98 to 0.99 throughout while shape falls 0.97, 0.90, 0.77, 0.35 at gates of none, 50, 70 and 90. Printed above each gate is the exact one-sided permutation p for the gap between the two kinds at that gate: 0.412, 0.034, 0.009 and 0.003. The lower is the null itself, all 5,005 ways of splitting these fifteen features six against nine, with both observed values marked: +0.009 ungated and +0.639 gated. Both are stated because either alone misleads, and Figure S5G is the control against the gate keeping only the strongest sites.

entry: (A) What is measured, and what is done with it. A probe labels lysines; a compound competes with the probe, and occupancy is the share of probe labeling it competes away. All 1,642,330 site × compound measurements in the three screens are shown, 8,019 of them (0.49%) reaching 60%. The median compound quantifies 6,332 lysines and engages 14. Right: the design for one compound, its engaged sites against the sites it was quantified at and left below the cut.

entry: (C) The measured model against the reproducibility ceiling. AUC 0.617 [0.594, 0.640] against a ceiling of 0.723 [0.706, 0.744] derived from agreement between independent halves of the same screen, a gap of 0.106; train AUC 0.619. 30,805 lysines on 6,201 proteins, 3,047 of them (9.9%) engaged by at least one compound. The ceiling drawn is the fragment screen's at twenty compounds per half, the deepest split the data support. That gap is reproducible signal the structure does not reach. It is not overfitting, since optimism is +0.002 AUC. The ceiling is still rising at the deepest split, so 0.723 is a lower bound. See also Figures S6B and S6D.

entry: (C, D) What each probe prefers, and which part of the charge effect belongs to which. Effects are standardized differences across proteins; intervals are 95% percentile bootstrap confidence intervals, resampling proteins (Methods). Cationic residues within 8 Å, d = +0.233, and net charge within 8 Å, d = +0.180, are the two features that separate the probes; the next largest, aromatic contacts at d = 0.118, does not. Zero of five pocket features and zero of nine shape features differ. The q values and the full twenty-two-feature test are in Figure 6B.

entry: (A) One reference atom, on both sides. The first version of this comparison measured union positions at Cβ and measured lysines at Nζ, and returned a separation of 2.256 against a control of 0.330, a 6.84-fold ratio that is an artifact of the mismatch. The three legitimate anchorings, both sides at Cβ, both modeled at Nζ, and both at Cβ under a symmetric convention, give 0.571, 0.535 and 0.583 against controls of 0.410, 0.331 and 0.407. The panel shows the artifact and the correction.
